intent.task: Determine every floor in 653 a-h and every bracket value in 654 a-d, retaining their exact order and both integer boundary cases.
intent.source_solution: Reused frozen FIRST solutions 653/654. From m<=x<m+1 the complete results are (1,263,27,0,-1,-1,-36,-11) and (26,0,-1,-281). In particular -1<=-0.4,-0.97,-0.54<0, -36<=-35.2<-35, and -11<=-10.7<-10. At integer arguments 27 and -281 the floor equals the argument; the defining lower bound is non-strict.
intent.unit_reason: Both original tasks evaluate the same floor function, once in prose and once in bracket notation. One complete two-row ordered result preserves all twelve values and contrasts negative nonintegers with positive and negative integers; it is not twelve isolated clicks.
limitations: 选择完整结果不能证明学习者独立书写了每个数的整数部分或其夹逼计算。

rationales.derivation: Deleting the decimal tail toward zero gives the displayed first row and second row: -0.4,-0.97,-0.54 become 0; -35.2 becomes -35; -10.7 becomes -10. Those integers exceed their negative arguments, so they cannot be floors.
rationales.misconception: Replace floor by truncation toward zero, leaving already integral arguments unchanged.

rationales.derivation: For each noninteger use the lower endpoint of its consecutive-integer interval; for 27 and -281 use the integer itself. This yields exactly both complete ordered rows recorded in the frozen source solution.

Choosing the least integer at least x gives ceilings: 1.8->2,263.4->264,0.345->1,26.4->27,0.33->1; negative nonintegers give 0,-35,-10 as displayed. For example 2>1.8, whereas a floor cannot exceed x.
rationales.misconception: Reverse the defining inequality and compute ceilings instead of floors.

rationales.derivation: Choosing the greatest integer strictly less than x preserves the correct noninteger entries but changes 27 to 26 and -281 to -282. The larger permissible integers 27 and -281 show the integer entries are wrong.
rationales.misconception: Use m<x instead of m<=x at integer arguments.

rationales.derivation: Taking the fractional part of |x| gives 0.64 for -0.64,0.27 for -6.27,0.01 for -100.01,7/11 for -7/11 and 0.8 for -134.8, with the other entries unchanged. The frozen subtraction from the actual negative floors instead gives 0.36,0.73,0.99,4/11 and 0.2.

rationales.misconception: Subtract truncation toward zero, rather than the lower integer floor.

rationales.derivation: Subtract the two complete floor rows in the frozen solution from their corresponding arguments. The negative noninteger entries are their positive complements to 1, the integer entries are 0, and -7/11+1=4/11 remains exact.

view.stem: 分别求 $x=65.4$ 和 $x=-65.4$ 时的整数部分与小数部分。哪一项完整给出了这两个数各自的有序对 $([x],\{x\})$？

intent.task: Determine both coordinates of the part pair for each of the two signed source values.
intent.source_solution: Reused frozen FIRST solution 657. Since 65<=65.4<66, the first pair is (65,0.4). Since -66<=-65.4<-65, the second is (-66,0.6), with -65.4=-66+0.6. Negating a noninteger changes the lower integer by the extra -1 and complements the nonzero fractional part to 1.
intent.unit_reason: The two source values form one coherent sign comparison. Each ordered pair must contain both parts of the same number; a paired complete result tests their relationship rather than four independent slots.
limitations: 结果对的识别不证明学习者独立写出了两个数的整数部分、小数部分及分解过程。

rationales.derivation: Truncating -65.4 to -65 and subtracting gives -0.4. Although -65+(-0.4)=-65.4, -65 is above the argument and -0.4 is not an allowed fractional part.
rationales.misconception: Use the signed decimal-tail decomposition as the integer/fractional decomposition.

rationales.derivation: Compute the positive pair (65,0.4), then negate only its first coordinate. The resulting second pair sums to -64.6 rather than -65.4 and uses the wrong lower integer.
rationales.misconception: Carry the positive decimal digits unchanged when negating the integer part.

rationales.derivation: Use the two consecutive-integer bounds recorded in the frozen solution, then subtract 65 and -66 respectively. The pairs (65,0.4) and (-66,0.6) satisfy both bounds and both sums.
Taking ceilings gives 66 for 65.4 and -65 for -65.4, then subtraction gives -0.6 and -0.4. Both second coordinates violate 0<=r<1.
rationales.misconception: Compute x as its ceiling plus a nonpositive residual.

view.stem:
把下列八个数分别写成整数部分与小数部分的和：

$21.43,\ 0.57,\ 14.5,\ -14.5,\ -0.068,\ -1.05,\ -5.44,\ -2\frac{9}{23}$。

每个数记为 $x=m+r$，其中 $m=[x]$、$r=\{x\}$。哪一项依次给出的八个有序对 $(m,r)$ 都符合这一分解？

intent.task: Preserve all eight source decompositions and distinguish a sum of arbitrary signed terms from the constrained integer-plus-fractional decomposition.
intent.source_solution: Reused frozen FIRST solution 658. The required pairs are (21,0.43),(0,0.57),(14,0.5),(-15,0.5),(-1,0.932),(-2,0.95),(-6,0.56),(-3,14/23). The negative mixed number means -(2+9/23)=-55/23; its floor is -3 and residual is (-55+69)/23=14/23. Each integer m satisfies m<=x<m+1, and each residual r is x-m in [0,1). These conditions establish uniqueness, not merely equality of the summed values.
intent.unit_reason: An ordered list of eight complete (integer part,fractional part) pairs preserves both summands and their relation to each original x. Defining the response as role-labelled pairs avoids treating arithmetically equal but invalid signed decompositions as equivalent answers.
limitations: 识别完整分解不证明学习者自主构造并书写了八个分解或负带分数的推导。

rationales.derivation: Use each frozen lower integer and subtract it from x. All eight sums recover the exact source values, all m are integers and all r lie in [0,1); for the mixed number -3+14/23=-55/23.

Truncation yields the first three correct pairs and the displayed negative signed tails for the remaining five. The sums still equal x, but every negative residual violates the fractional-part range; for -0.068 the proposed m=0 also exceeds x.
rationales.misconception: Assume that writing an integer and a signed decimal/fraction tail is sufficient, without the floor and nonnegative-residual conditions.

rationales.derivation: Apply the positive decomposition to |x| and attach a minus sign only to its integer coordinate. For example (-14,0.5) sums to -13.5, and (-2,9/23) sums to -37/23, rather than the corresponding negative source values.
rationales.misconception: Negate the integer digits but retain a positive tail from the absolute value.

rationales.derivation: Choose ceil(x) as m and set r=x-m. This gives 22 with -0.57,1 with -0.43,15 with -0.5 and the displayed five negative-case pairs. Every source value is nonintegral, so every displayed r is negative.
rationales.misconception: Decompose using the upper integer and a nonpositive residual rather than the floor and fractional part.

intent.source_solution: Reused frozen FIRST solution 659. For each integer n, all admissible examples are x=n+t,0<=t<1, i.e. [n,n+1). The six families are [14,15),[1,2),[0,1),[-1,0),[-5,-4),[-10,-9). Subtract -5 to obtain 0,0.25,0.9; all members lie in [-5,-4), so all three floors equal -5.

rationales.derivation: Permitting t=1 in x=-10+t admits -9 alongside -10 and -9.5. But [-9]=-9, so including the right endpoint makes the complete group invalid.
rationales.misconception: Replace the admissible half-open interval by a closed interval at its upper endpoint.

rationales.derivation: The three members themselves are t=0,0.4,0.9 in [0,1); each has floor 0.
Relative to -1 the offsets are 0,0.6,0.9 in [0,1). Thus -1,-0.4,-0.1 all lie in [-1,0) and have floor -1.
Allowing x=14+t with 0<=t<=1 admits 15. Its floor equals 15 rather than 14, although the other two group members qualify.

rationales.derivation: For a negative target, mistakenly form n-t with t=0,0.25,0.9. This produces the displayed group; -5.25 and -5.9 are in [-6,-5) and have floor -6.

Truncating -1.4 and -1.9 toward zero gives -1, but both actually lie in [-2,-1) and have floor -2. The integer -1 alone qualifies.

rationales.derivation: The offsets from -10 are 0,0.5,0.9 in [0,1), so all three members lie in [-10,-9) and have floor -10.

view.stem: 已知实数 $x$ 的整数部分分别等于 $8,\ 1,\ 0,\ -1,\ -17$。哪一项按这个顺序给出了每种条件下 $x$ 的完整取值集合？

intent.task: Determine all five complete real preimages of the specified floor values, including both endpoint decisions for each.
intent.source_solution: Reused frozen FIRST solution 660. [x]=n iff n<=x<n+1. Substitution of 8,1,0,-1,-17 gives [8,9),[1,2),[0,1),[-1,0),[-17,-16). At x=n the equality holds; at x=n+1 the floor becomes n+1 and fails. Every intermediate real, not just an integer sample, belongs.
intent.unit_reason: A complete five-target interval map is one coherent inverse-function result. It assesses full sets and endpoints, rather than ten isolated endpoint clicks or five sample witnesses.
limitations: 完整区间列表的识别不能证明学习者独立书写了集合表示与端点理由。

rationales.derivation: Using n<x<=n+1 produces all five displayed intervals. It excludes every valid x=n and includes every invalid x=n+1; for example 9 is included under floor 8 despite [9]=9.
rationales.misconception: Reverse the included and excluded endpoints of the floor preimage.

rationales.derivation: Replacing x<n+1 by x<=n+1 closes each right endpoint. The added values 9,2,1,0,-16 have floors 9,2,1,0,-16, not their respective requested floors.
rationales.misconception: Read the upper bound of a floor interval as non-strict.

rationales.derivation: Apply n<=x<n+1 to each of the five given n. The left integers 8,1,0,-1,-17 satisfy their own conditions, and the next integers do not; all five sets are exactly the displayed half-open intervals.
Using n<x<n+1 drops the five lower endpoints. Yet [8]=8,[1]=1,[0]=0,[-1]=-1,[-17]=-17, so every displayed set is missing a required solution.
rationales.misconception: Apply the noninteger-only strict lower bound even when x itself is an integer.

Closing both intervals yields [3,4] and [-3,-2], adding x=4 and x=-2. Their floors are 4 and -2, so the two upper filled points are invalid.

view.stem:
完成下面两组计算，并比较一般情况下的小数部分。

当 $x=3.7$ 时，依次求 $\{x\},\ \{x+4\},\ \{x-12\}$；当 $x=-7.4$ 时，依次求 $\{x\},\ \{x-50\},\ \{x+13\}$。

一般比较中，$x$ 为任意实数，$n$ 为任意整数，包括零与正、负整数。哪一项同时给出了两组的全部数值和对所有这些 $x,n$ 成立的关系？

intent.task: Assess all six numerical results and the full universal comparison for arbitrary real x and arbitrary integer n, preserving each shift and argument order.
intent.source_solution: Reused frozen FIRST solution 662. At x=3.7 the actual arguments are 3.7,7.7,-8.3 with floors 3,7,-9 and fractional parts (0.7,0.7,0.7). At x=-7.4 the arguments are -7.4,-57.4,5.6 with floors -8,-58,5 and fractional parts (0.6,0.6,0.6). If m=[x], adding any integer n to m<=x<m+1 gives m+n<=x+n<m+n+1, hence [x+n]=[x]+n and {x+n}=x+n-([x]+n)={x}. The proof covers integer/negative x and zero/negative n, not merely the samples.
intent.unit_reason: Both numerical triples and the universal relation express one integer-translation structure. One complete combined result prevents six arithmetic clicks or a law-only item that is handed its numerical evidence as solved stem data.
limitations: 不能证明学习者独立书写了六次计算或从定义构造了一般比较的论证；全部数值和全称量词仍被判断。

rationales.derivation: Holding [x] fixed when adding n gives (x+n)-[x]={x}+n, the displayed general relation. For x=3.7,n=4 it predicts 4.7 instead of 0.7, so the relation is false even though both displayed sample triples are right.
rationales.misconception: Assume the floor remains unchanged by integer translation, and add n directly to the fractional part.

rationales.derivation: In the negative-x sample use truncation floors -7,-57 for -7.4,-57.4, giving -0.4,-0.4; 5.6 still gives 0.6. The first two residuals are not fractional parts, so the whole result is false despite its correct general relation.
rationales.misconception: Use signed tails for the negative initial sample rather than the difference from its lower integer.

rationales.derivation: Reuse the two frozen complete triples and the integer-translation proof [x+n]=[x]+n. Subtraction cancels n for every real x and every integer n, including integer x and nonpositive n.

Extract fractional parts from absolute values: |-8.3| gives 0.3,|-7.4| and |-57.4| give 0.4, while positive 3.7,7.7,5.6 keep 0.7,0.7,0.6. This produces the displayed triples, which disagree with the source definition on their negative arguments.
rationales.misconception: Drop minus signs before computing the sample fractional parts; appending the true general law does not repair the wrong numerical results.

view.stem: 需要分别举出几个小数部分为 $0.9,\ 0.02,\ 0$ 的数。下面每项给出一个指定小数部分和一组数。哪些项中的数全部具有所指定的小数部分？选出所有成立的项。

intent.task: Preserve all three open fractional-part example requests, including valid positive/negative examples for nonzero targets and negative/zero/positive integers for target zero.
intent.source_solution: Reused frozen FIRST solution 663. For r in [0,1), {x}=r iff x=k+r for k in Z. The complete families here are {k+0.9:k in Z},{k+0.02:k in Z}, and Z. Frozen witnesses for 0.9 are 0.9,1.9,-0.1,-1.1; for 0.02 they are 0.02,1.02,-0.98,-1.98; for 0 they are -2,-1,0,1,2. The floors of each nonzero-target witness list are 0,1,-1,-2, giving the requested residual each time. A zero fractional part is equivalent to x being an integer.
intent.unit_reason: Native multiple judges complete proposed groups of several witnesses. All targets have valid groups, and the discrete translated families, negative convention and integer-zero boundary are retained without per-example clicks or framing one finite witness set as exhaustive.
limitations: 自主构造各小数部分对应的多个数及自主验证示例的能力未被观察；只识别已给整组示例。
有限示例不被声称为全部解集；参数所在整数集合不被限制为非负整数。

rationales.derivation: Negating the two positive witnesses while retaining their apparent decimal digits produces the displayed group. But -0.9-(-1)=0.1 and -1.9-(-2)=0.1, so its negative members do not have fractional part 0.9.
rationales.misconception: Assume negation preserves the fractional digits, equivalently compute the fractional part of |x|.

rationales.derivation: The four values are k+0.02 with k=0,1,-1,-2. Their floors are those integers, so every difference is exactly 0.02.
Rounding every number to an integer before taking its fractional part would report 0 for all five entries. The actual last value 2.5 has floor 2 and fractional part 0.5, so the group is not valid.
rationales.misconception: Round away the given noninteger value before applying the fractional-part operation.

rationales.derivation: The four values are k+0.9 for k=0,1,-1,-2. Subtracting those floors gives 0.9, including -0.1-(-1) and -1.1-(-2).
All five entries are integers, so each equals its own floor and has residual 0. Negative integers and zero qualify as well as positive integers.
Attach minus signs to the two positive witnesses while preserving the apparent tail 0.02. The actual negative differences are -0.02-(-1)=0.98 and -1.02-(-2)=0.98, so the group fails.
rationales.misconception: Treat a negative number's fractional part as the unsigned decimal tail of its absolute value.

rationales.derivation: The frozen intersection is (0,1). Interchanging the solid C and dashed D curve identities makes C appear higher on the negative side and lower on the positive side; translating those misidentified heights produces exactly the reversed strict intervals in this report. Actual image labels and the frozen negative/positive anchors give the opposite order.
rationales.misconception: Swap the solid and dashed curve identities while reading relative heights, then transfer that swapped order consistently to the inequalities.

rationales.derivation: The intersection coordinates and both side orders agree with the frozen solution and the rendered graph. Treating a strict inequality as allowing the intersection adds x=0 to each open half-line, producing the two displayed closed endpoints. At the crossing the two heights are equal, so zero is in neither strict solution set.
rationales.misconception: Include the equality crossing in both strict height-comparison solution sets.

rationales.derivation: Read the common point on the vertical axis at height 1 as (0,1), so equality has the sole x-coordinate 0. The negative-side dashed curve is above the solid curve, and the positive-side solid curve is above the dashed curve. Translate those heights into the two open half-lines, exclude equality from both strict cases, and retain all noninteger real x on each side. These readings agree with the existing frozen ratio proof; no source solution is redone.

Reverse the coordinate order when reading the true crossing (0,1), reporting (1,0). Use the incorrectly read horizontal coordinate 1 as the equality solution and as the boundary separating the lower-left and higher-right regions. This produces exactly {1}, (1,infinity) and (-infinity,1), but the visible crossing lies on x=0, not x=1.
rationales.misconception: Read an ordered coordinate pair as (vertical,horizontal), then partition the solution sets at the resulting wrong x-coordinate.
